items.preText:
lunch: "what's the bionic man thing on Gills face by his eye?" -- It's an AI-led wearable created by an Indian startup to track stress levels, monitor blood flow, and give a variety of insights. The two teams walk out amid a traditional welcome from the locals. Kids line up in front of the players too. Call it annoying or the peril of the modern age, but the youngster in front of Virat Kohli also has a 360-degree camera in his hand for some social media content. Anyway, here's India's national anthem, delivered by the young members of a local choir. Sweet, unique rendition. That is followed by NZ's. ranjith: "@ Kartik. I see this as an opportunity to test Gurnoor, Anshul and Nabi and feel that each should get at least 3 chances in this series! " Kartik: "One do the worst India bowling lineups I've seen in a long time. Absolutely ridiculous to not play Reddy and Siraj. " 3.05pm India have picked four frontline quicks, with Axar Patel and Naman Dhir offering spin. The bigger test will come once the ball gets older. Gill has spoken about using height and pace to make scoring difficult in the middle overs, when there may be less movement through the air.

That thinking is relevant to Gurnoor Brar, one of the taller quicks India have been keen to look at ahead of the 2027 World Cup. Gill says bowlers who can hit the right areas at 140 kph or more can make batters work harder, especially on a surface with bounce. Today is an early chance to see how that approach looks in New Zealand conditions.

New Zealand's middle order has plenty of experience to call on if the new top three are tested. Daryl Mitchell has been one of the most prolific ODI batters of this decade, averaging 57.36 since 2020, and four of his nine hundreds have come against India. Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips follow him, giving the hosts a chance to rebuild or counterattack depending on how the first spell goes. Prasanna S: "While Gill's assessment is right "The conditions here are going to be similar to SA" does this mean Kuldeep is going to continue to warm up the bench. He didn't get a game in England ODIs and for some reasons (small ground, conditions, combinations) he keeps getting sidelined outside India. If he's in plans for 2027 WC India must play him in SENA conditions somehow. " That was a very short chat with the captains, possibly to let all involved get into their warm-ups swiftly. We'll have the XIs shortly for the full line-ups.

India: Shubman Gill (capt), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (wk), Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh.

New Zealand: Tim Seifert, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (wk), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner (capt), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner. Dhairya: "Any idea why Siraj is not playing today!? Any injury or just break after recently concluded 4 days A game? " -- Probably just the break. 2.55pm The coin goes up in the air, and it's India who have won the toss. India will bowl first.

Gill: "We'll bowl first, bit of overcast weather, and in case there's a reduction of overs, it's good to chase. The conditions here are going to be similar to SA (where the WC is happening) compared to some other places. We are going with Anshul, Auqib, Gurnoor, Arshdeep as the bowlers with Naman and Axar as the allrounders."

Santner: "We've got to go again on another good pitch. With the schedules, there's been a bit more rotation. Conway is not playing today - Seifert, Young and Nicholls will be up top." Toss coming up soon at 2.50pm local; start confirmed for 3.10pm. Importantly, no overs lost. Shubman Gill and Mitchell Santner are in the middle waiting for the broadcasters to go live for the coin flip. Prasanna S: "This NZ series I would expect Gurnoor to solidify his place. He has gotten many opportunities in ODIs and despite promise yet to put his hands up as a leading contender for 3rd pacer slot. Another ok or less series, feel his time may be running out if Prasidh gets fit and Arshdeep with his experience as well." -- Auqib Nabi is also in this squad, and his swing-bowling abilities makes him a tempting option in these conditions. Abhipray: "Any update on toss time/inspection time/expected start time? " -- Not yet, but you'll know as soon as we do! For what it's worth, India have just jogged out for their training... and that means the crowd has found its voice over here! While we wait to learn about the toss time, here's something: do you know about Narotam "Tom" Puna, the first Indian-origin cricketer to play Test cricket for NZ? Born in Surat, British India, he was the 111th man to play Tests for NZ. Hiis grandchildren represented NZ in hockey and football too. His great grand-daughter is going to be a flag-bearer today once we have the national anthems. Hat tip to "The Guru" from our feedback section for sending me down this rabbit hole. Speaking of national anthems, we're on the right track for the coin-flip etc to happen sometime soon since the pitch has been uncovered and the ground is now enjoying some sunlight. The umpires are also inspecting the ground conditions. Kaz: "I will call it early, my prediction is 4-0 to Kiwis with 1 washout, Indias recent ODI against big teams have been poor, very weak bowling line-up, harsh but fair" Mallik: "Good Morning from India. Love to see Indian pacers and Kuldeep performing well. I also want to see Indian middle order getting more time in the middle and happy to see Ro-Ko just scoring just 50s and not centuries to give middle order that chance" 2.30pm It should've been toss now, but clearly not, with the main strip still covered and some droplets on the broadcasters' camera still not wiped off. Eden Park, today's venue is a rugby ground at heart, and it shows. The rectangular layout gives it a look unlike most cricket venues, with unusually short straight boundaries and pockets behind the wicket that are shorter still. Batters will be tempted to hit straight, but the ground's dimensions also make field-setting a puzzle: deep backward point can be around 60 metres from the bat, while deep third is under 50. Add Auckland's swirling wind, and even catching can become an adventure. Here's an analysis on what batters, bowlers and captains could do at this fascinating venue. 2.25pm New Zealand's plans have taken an early hit: Devon Conway is out of the opener after a concussion in a training-ground collision with Matt Henry. Tim Seifert is the likely replacement, though Henry's place is still uncertain. With Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman also missing, the hosts have decisions to make around their top order.

Eden Park should offer a different challenge from the T20Is. New Zealand made 259 here on Friday in the T20I, but the ground's ODI record is 340, set in 2007. The last two ODIs here under lights ended with teams bowled out for 150 and 76. The pitch is expected to offer bounce, and New Zealand will hope for some movement for the quicks. The dimensions add another layer. The straight boundaries are only about 52 to 55 metres from the centre of the pitch, while the pockets behind the wicket are even shorter. Batters will be tempted to go straight, but bowlers and captains will need plans for the unusual angles. With the 2027 World Cup in view, both sides will be looking for clues about their combinations and tactics on a surface that may reward pace and bounce. 2.15pm Niranjan Bhanda: "What a series we will be having this fortnight here in NZ! Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are absolutely loving to score some runs under their belt. Indian bowlers has been under the pump for a recent time Can they bounce back strongly here in NZ? Hyped" India's ODI top order is expected to look very different from the left-hand-heavy combination they used in the T20Is. Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli are all right-handers, giving India a more familiar shape at the top. Gill, meanwhile, is still looking for his first away series victory as captain.

Ishan Kishan adds a different sort of flexibility to the squad. He can open, keep wicket or bat in the middle order, and his recent T20I form has been sharp. With the World Cup still a year away, this tour is a chance for India to see how many of those roles he can cover. Karthik Krishnaswamy, our man at the venue, says that there was a light drizzle on not long back but it has stopped. That's a positive. Let's hope we are on for an on-time start. *fingers crossed* 2pm local: The visitors surged ahead in the T20I series only for the hosts to make a respectable comeback and end on 3-2. Now we get onto the ODI series where some personnel change, the tactics shift as well, and with an ODI World Cup around 12 months away, the focus now moves to the serious part of this tour. Welcome to New Zealand vs India from Auckland, my name is Sreshth Shah and joining us soon is Deivarayan Muthu.
